system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is that geopolitical conflict and high-profile political interventions are directly disrupting global energy supply and trade, producing sharp price and risk-allocations in oil, diesel, shipping and related markets. Attacks in the Middle East, continuing Russia–Ukraine dynamics, and abrupt policy or rhetoric (notably Trump’s diesel/‘energy ceasefire’ moves) create feedbacks across markets, currencies, safe-haven assets and regional security responses. The result is elevated market volatility, logistical strain (tankers, airports), and policy and diplomatic scrambling with spillovers into gold, equities and macro forecasts.
system_description.scope: The open system includes state and non-state military actors, national governments and political leaders, energy producers and refiners, global oil and diesel supply chains (production, shipping, ports, refineries), commodity and financial markets (oil, diesel, FX, gold, equities), major media and policy institutions that transmit information, and short-term market & security feedback loops active during this news window.
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic order (international security–economy complex) encompassing geopolitics, global trade, and international financial markets.
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and investor sentiment (equities, bonds, FX, safe havens)
International diplomacy and security architectures (NATO, regional coalitions, bilateral talks)
Maritime shipping & logistics (tankers, ports, insurance, routing)
Domestic politics and policy-making (elections, executive statements, regulatory moves)

variables.name: Geopolitical conflict intensity
variables.description: The aggregate intensity and frequency of armed clashes, strikes, and hostile incidents among state and non-state actors affecting regional stability.

variables.name: Policy rhetoric intensity
variables.description: The volume, prominence and aggressiveness of political statements and public policy messaging that influence expectations about conflict and economic policy.

variables.name: Energy supply disruption
variables.description: The ongoing rate at which energy production, refining, or transport is interrupted or constrained relative to baseline capacity.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: The magnitude and frequency of short‑term price fluctuations in crude oil markets.

variables.name: Diesel supply level
variables.description: The available inventory and immediate deliverable quantity of diesel fuel across markets and storage points.

variables.name: Refinery utilization rate
variables.description: The proportion of refining capacity currently operating and producing refined petroleum products.

variables.name: Shipping logistics delay
variables.description: The average added transit time and queueing delays in maritime and port logistics for energy cargoes.

variables.name: Tanker attack risk
variables.description: The perceived probability and expected frequency of hostile actions against energy shipping and port operations.

variables.name: Market risk aversion
variables.description: The prevailing investor preference for safety over return, reflected in willingness to sell risky assets and buy safer ones.

variables.name: Safe-haven asset demand
variables.description: The flow rate of capital reallocating into assets perceived as stores of value during uncertainty (e.g., gold, certain bonds, cash).

variables.name: Currency volatility
variables.description: The amplitude and frequency of exchange-rate movements for major currencies relevant to trade and energy pricing.

variables.name: Market liquidity
variables.description: The ease and depth with which assets (commodities, securities) can be bought or sold without large price impact.

variables.name: Information flow intensity
variables.description: The speed, volume and salience of news and data dissemination about geopolitical, energy and market developments.

variables.name: Policy coordination level
variables.description: The degree of alignment and joint action among governments and regulators in responding to geopolitical and market shocks.

variables.name: Trade flow volume
variables.description: The rate and quantity of internationally traded energy commodities moving through global supply chains.

variables.name: Infrastructure damage rate
variables.description: The pace at which critical energy and transport infrastructure becomes incapacitated or requires repair due to attacks, accidents or disasters.

catalysts.title: Fraying of Trump–Russia diesel deal
catalysts.description: Uncertainty and reversal around Trump's announced diesel-supply arrangement with Russia, altering expectations about Russian diesel exports and peace leverage.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump announces Ukraine energy ceasefire'; 'Oil rises as Trump’s "energy ceasefire" frays'; 'Why Trump’s Diesel‑Supply Deal With Russia Won’t Ease Fuel Prices Much'.

catalysts.title: Continued Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
catalysts.description: Ongoing Houthi strikes targeting Saudi airports cause casualties and closures, disrupting regional transport and raising security risks for energy logistics.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Houthi strike on Saudi airport kills 12'; 'Houthis attack Riyadh airport'; 'Saudi capital's airport to remain shut this week'.

catalysts.title: Elevated tanker rates and freight squeeze
catalysts.description: Rising tanker rates and longer voyages due to attacks and rerouting worsen crude distribution, creating regional barrel surpluses and shortages.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Oil Tanker Rates Surge Amid Rising Attacks, Longer Voyages'; 'Americas have glut of heavy oil due to freight squeeze; Asia, Europe scramble for barrels'.

catalysts.title: Riyadh airport closure this week
catalysts.description: Saudi capital airport remaining shut for the week forces cancellations and limits attendance at regional energy meetings, reducing coordination and information flow.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Saudi capital's airport to remain shut this week as airlines cancel services'; 'BP not able to attend Riyadh energy conference after airport attack.'

catalysts.title: EU considers oil & gas windfall tax
catalysts.description: EU deliberations on windfall profit taxes for oil and gas producers could change producer incentives and investor sentiment amid high prices.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EU looking at oil and gas windfall profit tax, as energy prices soar.'

catalysts.title: Iran's pending reply on Hormuz proposal
catalysts.description: Iran's forthcoming reply to a U.S. response on a Hormuz security proposal could either ease or inflame tensions affecting shipping in the Strait.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran says it will reply to US response on Hormuz proposal once review over.'

catalysts.title: Panama quakes risk to Canal operations
catalysts.description: Strong quake and numerous aftershocks in Panama raise short‑term risk to Panama Canal infrastructure and global shipping schedules.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Panama suffers over 200 aftershocks after Friday's 7.7‑magnitude earthquake'; 'Magnitude 6 earthquake strikes Panama.'

catalysts.title: Renewed Russia–Ukraine strikes escalate
catalysts.description: Ongoing Russian strikes in Ukraine continue, sustaining higher market risk premia and upward pressure on oil prices tied to conflict concerns.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Oil Climbs as Fighting Flares in Middle East, Ukraine'; 'S&P 500, Nasdaq Slip as Oil Rises on Russia Strikes in Ukraine'; 'Russian strike on Kyiv residential building'.

catalysts.title: Chinese live‑fire drills near Taiwan monitored
catalysts.description: Taiwan monitoring a series of Chinese live‑fire drills heightens regional tensions with potential short‑term impacts on shipping and trade flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Taiwan says it is closely monitoring a series of Chinese live‑fire drills.'
